correctness.rationale: The graphs have the stated adjacency definitions. Exhaustive enumeration checks all 2^16 masks and all 32 forbidden triangles per graph. The deterministic augmented matching has 4,466 and 3,658 pairs and globally acyclic Hasse digraphs of respectively 8,951 and 7,343 vertices. Dropping the empty-face pair leaves one critical zero-cell and cells only in degrees five and six. Exact signed gradient elimination generates boundary shapes 5x14 and 21x6 with maximal unimodular minors +1 and -1. Thus all integer Smith factors are units; the resulting one-vertex 5/6-dimensional CW complexes split into nine 6-spheres or fifteen 5-spheres because dimension-six attachments to wedges of 5-spheres are determined by degrees. Independent direct mod-two ranks of the unreduced simplicial boundary matrices confirm the ranks. All source paths in the row are self-contained.

evidence: Ghosh–Selvaraja Theorem 3.3 establishes shellability for t-diamond-free chordal graphs, and Theorem 4.2 treats constructed clique attachments; neither is an exact general homotopy classification for these graphs.
Both test graphs contain induced chordless 4-cycles: vertex masks (0,1,2,3) for Shrikhande and (0,1,4,5) for the rook graph.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A sufficient shellability theorem on a chordal subclass cannot cover these nonchordal graphs. Knowledge of t=2 or neighborhood/Čech homotopy gives no implication to the different t=3 vertex-set complex without an additional theorem; none was identified.

originality.rationale: The exact integral pair of homotopy classes for the triangle-free vertex-set complexes is not implied by the inspected t=3 shellability theorems or the t=2 independence complexes of these graphs. The literature and available published-research searches included exact graph names, the triangle-hypergraph/Stanley-Reisner reformulation, both sphere dimensions and multiplicities, and broader clique-free statements. No equivalent or dominating claim was located. This is a best-knowledge originality finding, not a uniqueness guarantee.

value.rationale: The Shrikhande/rook pair is the canonical nonisomorphic strongly regular pair with the same (16,6,2,2) parameters and exactly the same number of graph triangles. At t=2 their homology differs in multiplicity but shares degree two; at t=3 the topology instead moves to two distinct degrees (six versus five) and has exact integral homotopy classifications. This provides a natural structural counterexample to determination of higher clique-free homotopy by strongly regular parameters, not an arbitrary parameter slice or numerical recomputation; the specific objects and topology have clear use in assessing graph invariants and three-clique hypergraph topology.
